assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new class of electronic matter, with edge and surface states protected by topology and later quantum-anomalous-Hall dissipationless edge transport. The prediction-then-measurement chain is unusually clean, and the experimental verification is central to the case.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the decisive theory of the quantum spin Hall state; Molenkamp's group made the original experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells; Xue's group realised the quantum anomalous Hall effect experimentally. Supplied credit supports a theory-plus-two-experiments trio, though the Kane-Mele-Bernevig-Zhang-Fu theory credit and the separate QAH sub-discovery overlap with other ballot entries, and Mele or Bernevig are not available in this entry.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many groups (HgTe, ARPES on Bi-based materials, QAH in magnetically doped films, and later MnBi2Te4). Interpretation is stable and the field is mature; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the theory credit (Kane versus Kane and Mele, plus Bernevig, Zhang, Fu) can be fairly limited to the supplied names.
Compound discovery: quantum spin Hall, 3D topological insulators and QAH may merit different recognition.
I rely on my own recollection of the historical record and have not verified priority independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and validated the mechanism recognised in 2013. It is an original experimental discovery made with instruments of extraordinary complexity, and it matters for our understanding of nature.
assessment.attribution: The collaborations number thousands, but the founding spokespersons and project leaders (Jenni, Della Negra, Virdee) are widely credited for conceiving and leading the detectors. Fair attribution remains difficult because the discovery rests on collaborative work and accelerator contributions, and the prize rules limit the credit to three persons.
assessment.maturity: Both experiments independently observed the boson in 2012 and have since measured couplings and decay channels consistently with the Standard Model. The result is firmly established and long mature.
uncertainties: The rules strain against recognising a collaboration; leadership roles may not be seen as the decisive original contribution.
Other individuals (for example the discovery-era spokespersons, analysis leaders, or accelerator builders) might be argued as more decisive.
Priority between detector conception and discovery analysis is not resolved by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene created a tunable platform for correlated insulators and superconductivity in a clean carbon system, a genuine opening of a new door in materials physics, combining a precise theoretical prediction with a striking experiment.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted flat bands at the magic angle in 2011; the Jarillo-Herrero group reported correlated insulating and superconducting states in 2018 with the device control that made the effect observable. The supplied trio matches the prediction and the original experiment well.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced across many groups and multiple moire systems, though the nature of the superconducting pairing and correlated states is still debated. Reasonably mature for the discovery itself, but the physical interpretation continues to develop.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and the full phase diagram remain contested.
Experimental sample variability may leave questions about what is intrinsic.
Other early contributors to twisted bilayer physics, such as the Dean, Kim or Yacoby groups, are not part of the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks are a new measurement instrument that reaches fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, opening doors to tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second. The invention is concrete and the impact on precision measurement is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clock; Ye brought the clock to the highest accuracy and stability. The two-person allocation is compact and clear, though contributions from other groups on neutral-atom clocks, and the frequency comb that precedes them, are recognised separately in 2005.
assessment.maturity: Independently demonstrated by several laboratories and compared across continents; well established. The coming redefinition of the second would make recognition well timed.
uncertainties: Credit overlaps with prior prizes for laser cooling, the frequency comb and ion clocks.
The final redefinition of the second has not yet occurred, so the societal benefit is partly prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of X-ray, optical and radio afterglows established that gamma-ray bursts are cosmological, a long-standing puzzle resolved by an original observation. It opened the door to the identification of hosts, redshifts and the burst-supernova connection.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX discovery of the X-ray afterglow (1997), which enabled the rapid localisations; Kulkarni's group obtained key optical and radio follow-up and the redshift evidence. The credit is plausible, but the optical discovery by van Paradijs and colleagues and the redshift measurement by Metzger et al. are not in the supplied names and complicate attribution.
assessment.maturity: Cosmological origin is firmly established and confirmed by Swift and later missions; the discovery is mature, although the case against it being old news may arise.
uncertainties: Allocation among the X-ray, optical and redshift discoveries is contested and the supplied names exclude some of them.
Whether this is one compound discovery or several parts needing different recognition is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Solid-state femtosecond lasers (Ti:sapphire and its mode-locking, notably through Kerr-lens and semiconductor saturable absorbers) made ultrafast pulses compact and robust, and underpin attosecond science and countless applications. This follows the instrument-enabled door logic of the 2023 prize.
assessment.attribution: Moulton developed the Ti:sapphire laser medium; Sibbett's group demonstrated Kerr-lens mode locking; Keller developed semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors for self-starting mode locking. The three roles are distinct and fit a three-person prize, although Spence, Kean and Sibbett's KLM paper authorship and other claimants complicate it.
assessment.maturity: Technology is universally adopted and mature; the discovery is not recent, so the question is why now and whether the invention rather than the science is prize-worthy.
uncertainties: Priority among Kerr-lens mode-locking contributors and the lens-effect observation is not clear to me.
Some may view this as engineering rather than a discovery, and part of the story was already honoured in 2018 chirped pulse amplification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED realised strong light-matter coupling with superconducting qubits and microwave resonators on a chip, enabling quantum readout and control and underlying modern superconducting quantum processors. The original demonstration is an experiment that opened new phenomena.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues supplied the key theory proposal (2004) and Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in the lab; Schoelkopf's group also developed transmon-based architectures. The supplied trio is well formed, though other contributors to circuit-based qubits (for example Nakamura, Devoret, Martinis) have a related history.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across many laboratories and now the basis of commercial devices. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits makes partial overlap relevant and could affect timing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics for superconducting circuit quantum phenomena may reduce room.
Separation of the strong-coupling demonstration from qubit design (transmon) is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atomic-resolution qPlus force microscopy, in particular with functionalised CO tips, imaged the internal bond structure of single molecules, a new view of matter at the atomic scale. As a microscopist I value the instrument and the observations it opened up.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl invented the qPlus sensor; Meyer and Gross demonstrated sub-molecular bond-resolved imaging in 2009. The supplied credit follows the instrument and its decisive application. Yet atomic force microscopy itself was recognised in 1986, and the committee would have to weigh whether this is an original discovery or a later, more refined realisation.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and reproduced, with stable interpretation of bond-order contrast, though some image artefacts are known. The field is mature for imaging but the broader scientific impact is less than the leading entries.
uncertainties: Whether this counts as a new invention or an improvement on the scanning probe methods already recognised.
Contributions of the IBM Zurich group beyond the three names and tip functionalisation priority are unclear to me.
